nameStory: The 'speckled' part of this lichen's name comes from the tiny dark dots scattered across its surface like pepper flakes on green cheese. These speckles are actually the lichen's reproductive structures called perithecia, which peek through the greenish crust like little black freckles.
description: Speckled Blister Lichen is a crusty, flat lichen that grows directly on tree bark like a living paint job. It forms thin, greenish patches that can spread several inches across the surface of its host tree. The lichen gets its 'blister' name from its slightly raised, bumpy texture that feels like tiny blisters under your fingertip. **Note: I have limited knowledge about this specific species and some details may be uncertain.**

idTips.label: Greenish crusty surface
idTips.description: Look for a thin, greenish to yellowish-green crust that lies flat against tree bark, feeling slightly rough like fine sandpaper when you run your finger across it

idTips.label: Black speckled dots
idTips.description: Tiny black dots (perithecia) are scattered across the surface like coarse black pepper - these are the key identifying feature and feel slightly raised to the touch

idTips.label: Blister-like texture
idTips.description: The surface has a slightly bumpy, blister-like feel with small raised areas that give it texture rather than being completely smooth

idTips.label: Bark-hugging growth
idTips.description: Forms tight patches that conform perfectly to the bark's texture, never peeling at the edges like some other crusty lichens
